correctness.rationale: Two vertices are adjacent exactly when their shore patterns are complementary, in which case adjacency is complete. Testing the open-neighbor condition on either side of each component forces one vertex in each pattern. The independent choices give count ∏N_ε=B^(2^(r−1)); a move must change exactly one coordinate of this choice vector, giving the Cartesian product of cliques, its degree, and diameter 2^r because every pattern has at least two choices. Factorwise codes are identified by their coordinate projections, so there are B. Their number of common pattern choices is the product of the per-factor counts of equal endpoints (each 0, 1 or 2). Expanding by these three cases gives the stated elementary-symmetric multiplicities, disjoint-code multiplicity, and minimum distance. Any complementary patterns prescribe one endpoint on each named shore, so two positions can always be preserved. Under the stated shore bounds the injective labels within each shore force a conflict for every noncomplementary pair, proving an exact worst case of 2^r−2. For r=2 these bounds are exactly the standing hypotheses, and the stated example follows.
